Below are some concerns in the patch set is covered in this design:
1. Your concern about setting the `redfish host inband interface name` in EM.

In new design, The ethernet interface name will be configured use option redfish-host-interfaces in BMCWeb. Because BMC Web has the IP Address of redfish request, which can be mapped to Interface Name uses the D-Bus interface of Network objects. It can also identify if the authenticated account is bootStrap account use.

2. Ed: "Considering that we today don't enforce group membership in pam, I see this as a significant change to current. Please comment on the existing mailing list and code reviews that are proposing to change this"

New design, does not create new usergroup, I suggest adding one readonly D-Bus property name `IsBootStrap` in `User.Attributes` D-Bus interface to identify the account is bootStrap. This info managed by `phosphor-user-manager` but is updated value while create bootstrap account in phosphor-host-ipmid. No PAM changing is required.

3. Ed: This will make the bootstrap interface available from interfaces that are NOT the host interface. I'm fairly certain you want to provide some way to note that a user is a bootstrap user?

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/68746/comment/9fbc568b_f438a9dc/

In new design, two new API in phosphor-host-ipmid will be added:
+ ipmiUserSetGroupAccess -> to set userGroup of bootStrap account to redfish only.
+ ipmiUserSetBootStrapAccount -> To see `IsBootStrap` in `User.Attributes` D-Bus interface to `True` for bootstrap account.

4. About getting the IP address of the `redfish host interface`
Ed: How will it do this? How do we ensure that there are no conflicts? What if there are two NICs with the same IP address? What if the NIC has ipv4 and ipv6?

Lots of questions here; I'm happy to see them answered in code, but just doing a string compare of an ip address isn't going to work for a security boundary.

New design, 
```
Use the options `additional-ports` and `additional-bind-to-device` to different
the out-of-band redfish request which will come from port 443 or 80 with the
inband redfish request. Example: Add `additional-ports=199` and
`additional-bind-to-device=usb0` to specify that the request to interface `usb0`
should using port 199. This will be additional constraints to the
`redfish-host-interfaces` above option.
```

5. Ed: How will it do this? There's no way to map a given user account to a given "off" signal.

When the property CurrentHostState of interface xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host of object /xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0 change from xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host.HostState.Running to other value. all bootstrap account will be removed.

6. Ed : WAAAAAY longer testing section needed here. This is making changes to a security boundary in a non trivial way.

I added 5 test cases in new design.

Does this include a password on D-Bus? What are security implications on OpenBMC?

The password will not is included in the D-Bus.
When phosphor-host-ipmid handle request "Get Bootstrap account` it will do below steps:
1. Create one user account such as openbmcRhi1.
2. Call `ipmiUserSetUserName` to create the linux account
3. Create random password.
4. Set the password for above user use `ipmiUserSetUserPassword`
5. Set call ipmiUserSetPrivilegeAccess to set the privilege
6. Call `ipmiUserSetGroupAccess` (new API) to set user group.

The flow is the same phosphor-host-ipmid handles ipmi command to create the account. So it is secure.

Why is this observation necessary?

Because we want to limit the bootStrap account privilege on only the Redfish Host Interface but not in out-of-band redfish request, ssh or Ipmi.
That why when one redfish requests with bootStrap account we need identify which interface that request come from.

What happened to the design-point of binding a separate bmcweb instance to a specific interface?

Mixing authentication domains in the one bmcweb process feels perilous.

Using one BmcWeb instance for redfish host interface use `BindToDevice` option in systemd can make sure the request from the Redfish host interface will be handle by that instance.
But to identify which instance supports authenticate use `bootStrap account`, the additional option `additional-support-bootstrap` is be added. Only the BMCWeb instance with this option is `true` will response for the redfish host interface request with bootStrap username.
